Each result.json records head 74112b4 with uncommitted true and skill_hash 1fdf0c9b..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the new words "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`". skills_listed is 83 for every run, against 209 in 2026-10-31-b. Each transcript shows one Read, of SKILL.md, and no reference file, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with no warning against a stand-in Decimal written there. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a row with a -02:00 offset), the top five with ties broken by customer id, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an amount with trailing text and a bad date. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 also return {:error, ...} for an unknown status and a non-string amount. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 accept an unknown status (listed under Parse external data) and raise FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it straight to Decimal.parse/1, which no listed rule covers, as 2026-10-31-b noted. The doctests of haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass against the stand-in; haiku-1 has none.

Rule changed since 74112b4, graded against the current text: only Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function changed, by one clause. The sentence that now decides the verdict is "A body that calls another function that can fail and works on its result makes that call the second step, chained with a second `<-` instead of a nested `case`; when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function." All four runs are clean by it: each puts the case on Decimal.parse/1 and the case on DateTime.from_iso8601/1 in a private function that returns {:ok, value} or {:error, reason}, and chains those functions with `<-`. The 2026-10-31-b violation (sonnet-1, a case nested inside a one-step `with` on string_field/2) did not recur, but the batch does not test the clause against that shape: all four runs match the required keys in the parse_order/1 head, so no run has a first fallible step before the parse. No draft in the transcripts nests a case inside a one-step `with` either.

Verdicts worth checking. Name a step: all four runs bind the parsed value and then return it, as order = %{ ... } / {:ok, order} (haiku-1 96-104, sonnet-1 109-117 and sonnet-2 105-113 with %Order{}, haiku-2 94-102 as row = %{ ... }), and sonnet-1 80-85 and sonnet-2 70-75 do the same with report. This replaces the tagged literal {:ok, / %{ ... }} that 2026-10-31-b held clean; sonnet-2's transcript shows Edits making the change after its first write. Each name is used once, but the rule's "It does not when it only renames a value used once" is about renaming a value that already has a form, and these name a multi-line literal, which "names a recognizable thing" covers, so all are held clean. If the rule means that any once-used binding fails, all four runs are violated on it.

Unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-31-b standard. Atoms: haiku-1 and haiku-2 keep the status as a string, so not exercised, and the unknown status goes under Parse external data, as 2026-10-31-check listed for its haiku-1. Lists: haiku-1 line 79 and sonnet-2 line 85 prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean because grouping, counting, a max and a sort with a tie-break do not depend on the order.
